design_decisions: Each replay starts in watching with mutationObserved true, matching a real watch after it has seen a mutation, and assigns a distinct timestamp so reducer duplicate suppression cannot hide a sample.
The delete-tail sample preserves the backend contract exactly: sync-preparing, update_in_progress true, settled true, no download, and no upload.
The post-game signatures are asserted before Task 2 so the phase-guarded reset behaviour remains a deliberate regression boundary.
A content-pending fixture uses the backend's UPDATE_NEEDED payload: sync-preparing and update_in_progress true, but settled false and no active transfer.

The reducer now selects the display status first, then independently resets or increments the settle count; this keeps a settled delete-only tail quiet while preserving the three-sample release guard.

test_changes: Set contentDownloadSample.update_in_progress to true so it matches active-transfer backend samples.
